body: The reproduction steps are inaccurate but it happens quite easily - it seems to occur when you arbitrarily select shader material(contains shader) in the Inspector, switch and reload scenes.
CC @Ivorforce. I have no idea why it crashes due to #103708, but I did bisect it to that.
Thanks for bisecting. That's suspicious indeed, I'll have a look.

The memory of `p_object` looks reasonable, but empty. I get a complaint on `is_class_ptr` call that the pointer is invalid and cannot be dereferenced. I suspect the object has already been deallocated at the time of the call.

```
(lldb) print obj->is_class_ptr((void *)20)

error: Execution was interrupted, reason: Attempted to dereference an invalid pointer..
The process has been returned to the state before expression evaluation.
```

I'm not sure why it didn't use to crash before the `cast_to` change, but it's possible the `reinterpret_cast` circumvented pointer sanity checks somehow.

Practically, especially considering it occurs quite rarely (I had to try for a solid 5 minutes until I triggered the crash), I suspect it's a race condition. Something is adding a callable, then the object is freed while the callable is executed. The object is handed out from `ObjectDB` during destruction, so the caller is none the wiser and henceforth handles an invalid pointer.
I'm not sure how to prevent this fully, since `ObjectDB` is inherently not thread safe in this regard. But we might be able to track down this one bug by avoiding destruction in one thread while it's still registered for a callback.

Edit: Tried to track down what the callable was, unfortunately lldb doesn't let me use `typeid` :(
But it must be something with two parameters, both of which get object args. I suppose `edit_item` would be the one, scheduled from `_open_editor_pressed`?

I do like the solution. It solves the problem in a straight forward manner.
Unfortunately, going by the comment, it may introduce some other regressions. Unless the comment is no longer relevant.

I think the crash may be caused by the object being destructed in a thread other than the main thread. Since callables are resolved on main, if both happen there the race condition shouldn't be possible. Perhaps that would be a more appropriate fix?

I found it also crashes with selected exported shader property from custom nodes. And this issue appears to be specific to `Shader`.
~I guess when executing the callable the resource's reference count had dropped to zero and was released, but the callable still held the pointer~. Maybe the editor maintainers knows more about it, and if the comment there still applies?

Taking a second look, it looks like `ObjectDB` may not even be involved at all. That would add the possibility of this happening within the same thread. 

> I guess when executing the callable the resource's reference count had dropped to zero and was released, but the callable still held the pointer. 

I was under the impression that it was the second parameter that was destructed by the time the callable was called. Parameters to callable_mp are converted to `Variant`, which holds refs for `RerCounted` object instances. Which should make it impossible for the resource to destruct before the call.

With #108548 it doesn't crash, but prints the errors:
```
ERROR: Parameter "p_editing_owner" is null.
   at: edit_item (./editor/editor_node.cpp:2537)
ERROR: Error calling deferred method: 'EditorNode::EditorNode::edit_item': Instance is null.
   at: _call_function (./core/object/message_queue.cpp:222)
```
So the issue is that the inspector was cleared and `EditorPropertyResource` was freed before `edit_item()` executes to open shader editor plugin. I can confirm it also occur with `TileSet` (I suspect this issue occurs with any resource that has an editor plugin).

My patch may be the correct fix. At the very least, I can no longer reproduce that issue(#23672) closed 6 years ago which originally necessitated the `call_deferred`.
